dedupe_keys.name: mining actionable patterns of road mobility from heterogeneous traffic data using biclustering

description: The implemented method discovers coherent local patterns in heterogeneous traffic observations, combining geolocated speed and loop-count information. It treats recurring congestion profiles across locations and time periods using speed limits, queue extent, delay and flow-related views. The Lisbon application examines statistical significance and interpretability of the recovered spatiotemporal associations. This is distinct from E 2 PAT, which detects emerging patterns using time differencing. The project catalogue connects both to the same thesis and source-data families, but does not establish identical algorithms, samples or one shared downloadable implementation. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with open document or data access and licence label cc-by-4.0. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened. The source establishes traffic-pattern analysis; a separate network-flow solver or forecast use is not asserted.
